notes:
Source: Australian_Financial_Services_APIOps_Cycles_Case_Study (1).docx, supplied by the user. Client anonymised. Engagement by APIsFirst with partner Osaango. Benefits are qualitative; no quantified delivery or business impact is claimed.

Four newly authored illustrative examples continue the fictional supplier-payment scenario. They demonstrate the canonical API Business Model, Business Impact, Capacity and REST canvases. They do not reproduce the supplied real reference set, and are not evidence of actual client artefacts or delivered capabilities. The business-model canvas names the provisional Supplier Payments API before its value proposition. Impact entries describe expected benefits and risks, not observed impact. Capacity entries explicitly identify a volume baseline to measure, a peak to test and service hours to agree; no traffic forecast or measured capacity is invented. REST request and response examples are illustrative only. Canonical templates: local apiops-cycles-method-data canvasData.json and localizedData.json, IDs apiBusinessModelCanvas, businessImpactCanvas, capacityCanvas, restCanvas.
